study type: Prospective, multicenter, international, randomized, parallel, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial
outcome: Composite of fetal and neonatal outcomes
cohort: 502 pregnant women with type 2 diabetes on insulin from 25 centers in Canada and 4 in Australia
finding: The addition of metformin to insulin in pregnant women with type 2 diabetes did not significantly affect the composite neonatal outcome but resulted in better glycemic control, reduced insulin requirements, lower maternal weight gain, fewer caesarean births, and lower neonatal adiposity, with a higher proportion of small-for-gestational-age infants.
mod_finding: Metformin-treated women had fewer caesarean births compared to the placebo group (53% vs. 63%, p=0.031).
birth_weight: Infants of metformin-exposed mothers had a lower mean birthweight compared to those in the placebo group (3156 g vs 3375 g, p=0.002).
